template.name: AI Agent Adoption Planning
template.summary: 48 questions to align intended work, expected value, authority and evaluation.

resolutionStates.label: Confirmed
resolutionStates.description: Use this as an accepted project premise.

resolutionStates.label: Provisional
resolutionStates.description: Use this for now, but keep it visibly open to revision.

resolutionStates.label: Not decided
resolutionStates.description: Leave this open. Do not let an AI silently fill it in.

resolutionStates.label: Ask for a proposal
resolutionStates.description: Request alternatives or a recommendation without treating one as chosen.

resolutionStates.label: Delegate within bounds
resolutionStates.description: Allow the implementer or AI to decide within the stated limits and report the choice.

resolutionStates.label: Does not apply
resolutionStates.description: Mark this question as outside the project.

messages.validation.provenanceRequired: Choose whose perspective this answer represents and who recorded it.
messages.validation.speakingRoleMismatch: The selected speaking role is not assigned to that participant.
messages.validation.inferenceUnconfirmed: An inferred answer must remain unconfirmed until an authorized person verifies it.
messages.validation.resolutionAuthorityRequired: Confirming this premise requires an authorized decision source.
messages.validation.exclusiveChoice: This option cannot be combined with other selections.
messages.validation.noteRequired: Add a short note to explain this selection.
messages.validation.selectionLimit: Reduce the number of selected options.
messages.review.authRuntime: Authentication is in scope, but the selected runtime may require an external or server component.
messages.review.paymentHandling: Payment-related data is in scope. Confirm who processes it and whether the project may store any of it.
messages.review.analyticsPrivacy: Analytics or telemetry is in scope. Recheck the privacy boundary, consent, and prohibited practices.
messages.review.agent.baseline: The expected reduction has no measured baseline. Define the current workload and measurement before claiming improvement.
messages.review.agent.authority: Answer-only scope and state-changing actions are both selected. Clarify whether the agent prepares an action or executes it.
messages.review.agent.review: The plan relies on human checkpoints without an assigned review arrangement. Define a responder and what happens while waiting.
messages.review.agent.release: Direct introduction is planned without representative evaluation evidence. Revisit the release criteria and initial exposure.

questions.prompt: What work should change, for whom?
questions.help: Give one real request, the desired deliverable and who uses it. Avoid goals such as simply introducing AI.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How should work start?
questions.help: Specify frequency, volume, deadlines and the boundary between one task and the next.

questions.prompt: What phase is this initiative in?
questions.help: For existing deployments, identify the behavior to preserve or change.

questions.prompt: What is outside this initiative?
questions.help: Name excluded decisions, users and workflows, and why they are excluded.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How is this work done today?
questions.help: Trace input → judgment → action → review → delivery, including informal coordination and exceptions.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: Where is the main observed bottleneck?
questions.help: Record evidence and who experiences the delay; distinguish a slow task from waiting for a decision.

questions.prompt: What evidence describes current performance?
questions.help: Specify period, sample size, workload, quality, human time and waiting time. Estimates remain estimates.

questions.prompt: How predictable are the tasks and exceptions?
questions.help: Give a routine case and a difficult case, including missing or contradictory inputs.

questions.prompt: Which benefit should take priority?
questions.help: Name the beneficiary. Faster output does not necessarily reduce total workload.

questions.prompt: Why would the proposed approach create that benefit?
questions.help: State the causal hypothesis, supporting evidence, assumptions and what would disprove it. A demo is not production evidence.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What measurable change would count as success?
questions.help: Specify baseline, target, period, denominator and measurement owner. Count review, corrections and escalations in total effort.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What must not worsen while pursuing the benefit?
questions.help: Define acceptable tradeoffs across quality, cost, speed, staff burden and user experience.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: Which approaches should be compared?
questions.help: Include the least complex viable approach; choosing no agent remains a valid result.

choices.label: AI suggestions reviewed by a person

questions.prompt: What may the system do without new approval?
questions.help: Separate generating a suggestion from changing an external system. State scope and limits in the note.

choices.label: Act after approval for each action

questions.prompt: What requires adaptive planning or tool selection?
questions.help: Give a case fixed automation cannot handle, or state that the need is not established.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What evidence supports technical feasibility?
questions.help: Identify tested systems, versions, data and constraints; distinguish vendor claims from your own evaluation.

questions.prompt: Whose expectations or workload may differ?
questions.help: Separate sponsor, frontline user, reviewer, recipient and affected non-users. Record disagreements as separate contributions.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: Who owns the outcome and approves changes in scope?
questions.help: Name roles for business results, system operation and final decisions; a supplier is not automatically the business owner.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: Who can handle reviews and exceptions, and when?
questions.help: Specify competence, volume, response time, coverage and what happens when nobody responds.

questions.prompt: What must a person receive when taking over?
questions.help: Include original request, actions already taken, evidence, uncertainty and safe next steps; define who acknowledges the handoff.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: Which sources may inform the work?
questions.help: Name authoritative sources, access owners, formats, freshness and missing information.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What kinds of data are involved?
questions.help: Describe categories without entering actual secrets or personal records into this questionnaire.

choices.label: Credentials handled through a protected mechanism

questions.prompt: Where may data and logs be processed or retained?
questions.help: Specify approved services, regions, retention, deletion, training use and who verifies the conditions.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What should happen when information is missing or conflicting?
questions.help: Define the boundary between a labeled hypothesis and a fact, and which gaps block action.

questions.prompt: Which systems and interfaces are needed?
questions.help: Record APIs or UI operations, read/write scope, service accounts, test environments and integration ownership.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What real-world changes must the system make?
questions.help: Distinguish preparing an action from executing it; add per-action limits.

questions.prompt: Which actions require whose approval?
questions.help: Map each action to a role, threshold, approval lifetime and record. Never treat silence as approval.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How will the allowed action boundary be enforced?
questions.help: Explain identity, least necessary access, tool validation, sandboxing and authorization checks outside model output.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What should persist between tasks?
questions.help: Specify purpose, ownership, retention, correction and separation of users or organizations.

questions.prompt: Which instructions prevail when premises conflict?
questions.help: Define sources of authority, versioning and who resolves disagreement. Keep quoted content distinct from instructions.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How are instructions inside retrieved content handled?
questions.help: Plan for prompt injection: untrusted content attempting to redirect actions, reveal data or expand permissions.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How will context pass between people, tools or agents?
questions.help: Define shared records, ownership, duplicate-work prevention and conflict resolution. Multiple agents are optional.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What failures would matter, and to whom?
questions.help: Use concrete cases: plausible wrong answers, omissions, duplicate actions, disclosure, delays or service outage.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What must never be delegated or executed?
questions.help: Record hard boundaries separately from preferences and identify who may revise them.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: When and how can execution be stopped?
questions.help: Define triggers, stop owners, action/time/spend limits, cancellation of queued work and safe state after stopping.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How will failures be detected and recovered from?
questions.help: Cover logs, backups, rollback, compensating actions, safe retries, manual fallback and an accountable responder.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What representative tasks will be used for evaluation?
questions.help: Include routine, difficult, incomplete, conflicting and hostile inputs, with expected results and access permission.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How will the proposed approach be compared fairly?
questions.help: Use comparable workload and quality criteria, include human correction costs and distinguish proxy scores from business outcomes.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What evaluation evidence exists now?
questions.help: Record version, date, sample size, observed failures and limitations; do not infer evidence from a plan.

questions.prompt: What conditions permit release or require rejection?
questions.help: Specify quality, effect, cost and boundary thresholds, decision owner and unresolved items that block release.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What execution environment and suppliers are allowed?
questions.help: Record deployment constraints, model/service choice criteria, availability, integration dependencies and portability.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What is the total cost limit and how will it be controlled?
questions.help: Include usage, tools, infrastructure, integration, review, correction, training and maintenance; specify per-task and recurring limits.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What must be observable during operation?
questions.help: Connect each metric or log to a recipient and response. Limit sensitive data in logs.

questions.prompt: Who maintains and revalidates the system?
questions.help: Cover model, prompt, tool, permission and data changes; keep versions, evaluation results and rollback paths.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: How should the first introduction proceed?
questions.help: Define users, workload, duration and exposure limits for the first stage.

questions.prompt: How will people learn and adapt their work?
questions.help: Define training, feedback, workload changes and an alternative for cases the agent cannot handle.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: What evidence allows expansion of scope or autonomy?
questions.help: Treat more users, data, tools or permissions as a new decision with an owner and evaluation, not an automatic reward for success.
questions.placeholder: Describe an example, evidence, boundaries and unresolved points.

questions.prompt: When will the plan be reviewed, reduced or stopped?
questions.help: Define dates and triggers, who decides, and how data, unfinished work and responsibilities return to people or another system.
